title: DNA repair: which pathway for which damage
caption: Proofreading corrects errors as DNA polymerase works. After replication, mismatch repair corrects mismatched bases that were missed; base excision repair removes single damaged bases such as oxidised ones; nucleotide excision repair removes bulky damage such as the thymine dimers that UV light causes; double-strand breaks are repaired by homologous recombination, which uses a sister chromatid as a template, or by non-homologous end joining, which can lose bases. The right-hand panel works through nucleotide excision repair on a short sequence: the gap is refilled using the other strand as the template, so the original sequence is restored.
alt: Left: four boxes of damage, each with an arrow to its repair pathway. Right: four steps of nucleotide excision repair on a twelve-base sequence: a thymine dimer joins two adjacent Ts, a section containing it is cut out, the gap is refilled using the opposite strand as the template, and ligase seals the strand with the original sequence restored.
description: Mismatch repair corrects mismatched bases missed by proofreading.
Base excision repair removes single damaged bases, such as oxidised bases.
Nucleotide excision repair removes bulky damage, such as thymine dimers caused by UV light.
Double-strand breaks: homologous recombination (sister chromatid as the template) or non-homologous end joining (can lose bases).
Steps of nucleotide excision repair: detect the distortion, cut out a section of the damaged strand, DNA polymerase fills the gap using the other strand, ligase seals it.
